name: What is the most expensive part of a kitchen addition?

mainEntity.name: What is the most expensive part of a kitchen addition?
mainEntity.text: What is the most expensive part of a kitchen addition?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most expensive part of a kitchen addition is usually the combination of structural work and utility relocation. Foundation, framing, load-bearing modifications, plumbing, electrical, HVAC, and any wall or roof tie-ins can quickly outpace the visible finish costs. In luxury projects, custom cabinetry, premium stone, and high-end appliances can also become major line items. The exact cost driver depends on the home’s condition and the amount of change required. If the new kitchen stays close to existing plumbing and utilities, finishes may take a bigger share of the budget. If the addition requires major reconfiguration, the invisible work can dominate the total cost. This is an important unanswered question because many homeowners focus on cabinets and countertops while underestimating the structural backbone of the project. A strong answer should clearly separate hard costs into structure, systems, and finishes so the reader understands where the money really goes.
acceptedAnswer.description: The most expensive part of a kitchen addition is often the structural and utility work, especially foundation, framing, plumbing, electrical, and major layout changes. Custom cabinetry, stone, and premium appliances can also be major cost drivers. The biggest expense depends on the home’s existing conditions and finish level.
